From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Harbourglass Ventures' "Seller Update" and Disclosure Letter dated 22 September 2026
**Status:** Privileged working draft – for review by the deal team and NSW-qualified counsel before any positions are communicated to the Seller.

## Overall assessment

The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. Read as a whole, the Seller Update does three things: (1) it collapses every protection the Buyer would normally rely on (fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, fraud) into a single low cap and short time limit; (2) it pushes three pre-Completion problems – Bluefen consent, Riverlark debt, Ironquay IP – past Completion so they become the Buyer's problems; and (3) it uses general data-room disclosure plus a "discoverable by the Buyer" knowledge clause to neutralise the warranties for every issue already flagged in DD. The Disclosure Letter is, to its credit, candid about what has *not* been done (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, no Ironquay payment, bonuses not in funds flow, incident investigation incomplete). That candour should be used against the Seller Update, not treated as disclosure against warranty.

The Disclosure Letter is also six weeks stale (22 September 2026; today is 4 November 2026). Everything below should be read on the assumption that a bring-down is required.

---

## Part A – Liability architecture (Clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5)

### A1. Fundamental and title warranties swept into the general cap – **reject outright**

The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity". This is the most important single point in the package.

- The Buyer is paying AUD 24,000,000 to acquire 100% of the shares. If title fails, the Buyer has lost up to the full price; a recovery capped at AUD 4,800,000 and time-barred after 18 months is not a remedy.
- There is no genuine administrative burden: a separate cap and period for fundamental warranties is one additional sub-clause.
- Market position (NSW private M&A): fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at 100% of price and surviving for 6–7 years (or the longest period permitted at law).

**Push back:** Fundamental warranties at 100% of purchase price, 6–7 years, excluded from de minimis/basket, and not subject to disclosure.

### A2. General cap at 20% (AUD 4,800,000) – **negotiate up, and secure it**

20% is at the low end for a deal of this size with known open issues. More importantly, the counterparty is Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd – a Pty Ltd vehicle that, post-sale, may hold nothing but the proceeds. A cap is only worth the covenant behind it.

**Push back:**
- Target 30–50% of price for general warranties; accept 20–25% only if (i) the carve-outs in A3–A5 are won and (ii) there is security for claims.
- Require an **escrow/retention** (e.g. 10–15% of price for 18–24 months) or a **guarantee from a substantive Harbourglass group entity**, or price in W&I insurance (noting known issues – Bluefen, Ironquay, DD-006 – will be excluded from cover and must be dealt with by specific indemnity anyway).

### A3. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (Cl 12.3/13) and "limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) – **reject**

These are drafting devices to drag everything into the 20% / 18-month box. Their combined effect would cap and time-bar:
- the Ironquay indemnity (Cl 11.1);
- any tax indemnity;
- any specific indemnities we obtain for DD-006, Riverlark, bonuses;
- claims for fraud or wilful concealment;
- claims under the price adjustment / debt-free cash-free mechanics;
- Seller's Completion obligations (delivery of share transfers etc.).

An exclusive-remedy/non-reliance clause purporting to exclude liability for fraud is unenforceable, and purported exclusion of liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law is of doubtful effect – but we should not rely on a court to fix the drafting.

**Push back:** Reverse the default. The limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Express carve-outs for: fundamental warranties; tax warranties and tax indemnity; all specific indemnities; fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; Completion obligations and price/leakage adjustments; costs of defending third-party claims. Non-reliance clause limited to pre-contractual representations and expressly preserving statutory rights.

### A4. Thresholds (Cl 12.2) – **adjust**

- De minimis AUD 25,000 and basket AUD 250,000 (~1.04% of price) are within range, but the basket is drafted as a **deductible** ("only the excess above the basket is recoverable"). Push for a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar).
- Add that **related or series claims aggregate** for de minimis purposes – relevant to Sandbar (3 × AUD 110,000) and any pattern of related losses.
- Thresholds must not apply to fundamental, tax, or specific indemnity claims.

### A5. Time limits (Cl 12.3/13)

- General warranties: 18 months is acceptable only if it captures at least one full audited accounting cycle post-Completion; 24 months is preferable.
- Tax: the later of 7 years and the expiry of the relevant ATO amendment period plus a margin.
- The Seller's statement that tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime" should be rejected. Tax needs a separate indemnity (uncapped or capped at price); IP warranties for an analytics business are core-value warranties and should carry at least a higher cap and longer period, particularly given the Ironquay ownership gap.

### A6. Clause 8.3 Buyer knowledge – **reject**

"No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter **discoverable** from the data room or public records" would:
- impute the knowledge of every adviser, not just the deal team;
- extend to constructive knowledge ("discoverable"), i.e. anything in the data room or on ASIC/PPSR, whether or not anyone actually read it; and
- combined with general disclosure (A7), extinguish every warranty touching an issue raised in DD – which is precisely where the risk is.

The Buyer has priced the deal on the warranties; the warranties should not disappear because the Buyer did its diligence.

**Push back:** Delete 8.3. Fallback: limited to *actual* knowledge of two or three named Buyer individuals, derived solely from matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter, and in any event not applying to the specific indemnities.

### A7. General disclosure of data room and public registers (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2) – **reject; require fair disclosure standard**

- General disclosure of "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room means a buried reference in any document qualifies every warranty.
- "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended (what records, which date?).
- DL 1.4 says nothing in the letter admits that any consent, payment or notice is required – the Seller wants the *facts* to count as disclosure but disclaims the *conclusions*. That is fine only if disclosure is limited to specific disclosures.

**Push back:** Disclosure effective only to the extent **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect on the warranty**. No general disclosure of the data room. Public searches limited to specified ASIC and PPSR searches against the Company on a stated date. Specific disclosures are made against specific numbered warranties.

### A8. Stale disclosure – **require bring-down**

Data-room cut-off 22 September 2026. Require: (i) warranties repeated at Completion; (ii) updated Disclosure Letter at Completion for new matters only, which does **not** qualify warranties for the purpose of a Buyer claim but gives the Buyer a termination right / price adjustment if material; (iii) Seller obligation to notify any breach discovered between signing and Completion.

---

## Part B – Pre-Completion issues the Seller is trying to push past Completion

### B1. Bluefen change-of-control consent (Cl 3/6.3; DD-002) – **highest commercial priority**

~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue, ~30% of the business. Change-control consent under clause 11.2 is subject to conditions in 11.3. The Disclosure Letter confirms **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions have been satisfied**.

Problems with the Seller's position:
- "Reasonable endeavours" is the weakest endeavours standard.
- Treating the condition as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's "written consent" alone ignores clause 11.3 – a conditional consent whose conditions are unmet is no protection; Bluefen could still terminate.
- Nothing says the consent must be unconditional or on terms acceptable to the Buyer; the Seller could obtain consent by agreeing adverse amendments.

**Push back:**
- Condition precedent for the **Buyer's sole benefit** (waivable only by the Buyer): Bluefen written consent, unconditional or on terms approved by the Buyer, plus evidence that all 11.3 conditions are satisfied, with no amendment to the Bluefen contract without Buyer approval.
- Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours), with Buyer participation in Bluefen discussions, and a sensible long-stop date.
- If the Seller resists a hard CP: price adjustment/earn-out holdback referable to Bluefen revenue, or a specific indemnity/retention if Bluefen terminates or reduces scope within 12–24 months by reason of the change of control.

### B2. Riverlark Bank facility (Cl 2/7; DD-003) – **reject "release following Completion"**

~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, change-of-control clause 8.1, discharge clause 9.2. The deal is debt-free/cash-free, yet the Seller proposes that the release follows Completion. Consequences if accepted:
- The Buyer acquires a company carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt and likely in change-of-control default from the moment of Completion.
- Riverlark's security (over company assets and possibly the shares – check DD-003 and PPSR) remains in place after the Buyer owns the company.
- No mechanism ensures the Seller ever funds repayment.

**Push back:**
- Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price via the funds flow: bank payout letter (figure as at Completion date) delivered pre-Completion; on Completion, Buyer pays the payout amount directly to Riverlark; delivery of executed deed of release, PPSR discharge and release of any share security as Completion deliverables.
- Any amount not discharged at Completion is Debt for the price mechanism and is deducted dollar-for-dollar.
- Confirm whether Riverlark consent is needed under 8.1 even for a Completion repayment (e.g. prepayment fees, break costs) – these are for the Seller's account.

### B3. Ironquay Development Studio – SOW3 Project Materials (Cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010) – **this is an IP ownership gap, not a AUD 180,000 payment issue**

DD-004 clause 7.3: Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment exist. Until paid, the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables. For an analytics company, that may be core product.

The Seller's indemnity "limited to the specific SOW3 payment" would, at most, reimburse AUD 180,000 – and under the Seller's A3 drafting would be subject to the 20% cap, basket and 18-month limit. It would not cover loss of ownership, third-party claims, injunctions, or re-development cost.

**Push back:**
- Completion deliverable / CP: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay (plus moral-rights consents from individual developers if not already in place).
- Independent verification (bank statements, Ironquay confirmation) of what is actually outstanding – the Seller itself notes DD-010 is not bank-verified.
- Specific indemnity broadened to all loss arising from the Company not owning, or Ironquay asserting rights in, the SOW3 Project Materials – outside the general cap/basket/time limits.
- If the fee is unpaid at Completion, it is Debt in the price mechanism.

### B4. Completion bonuses – DD-005 (AUD 420,000) – **must go into the funds flow**

The bonuses are a **Company** liability triggered by Completion. "A matter for the Seller and not separately itemised" means, in practice, the Company (now Buyer-owned) pays them after Completion. In addition, the Disclosure Letter confirms on-costs are unquantified: superannuation (12% from 1 July 2025), NSW payroll tax (5.45% above threshold), and any leave or workers-comp loading – realistically AUD 480,000–500,000 all-in.

**Push back:**
- Bonuses plus all on-costs are **Transaction Expenses/Debt** deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller through the funds flow at Completion with evidence of payment.
- Review DD-005 terms: who are the recipients, is "continued employment" a condition at Completion or for a period after (if after, the Company bears a contingent liability and retention risk), and is there any claw-back.
- Warranty that there are no other transaction-related payments, change-of-control entitlements, or accelerated equity.

---

## Part C – Operational and compliance matters characterised as immaterial

### C1. DD-006 export/privacy incident – **specific indemnity required; "not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion**

Download link sent to an unintended external email address; ~1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps. The Seller does not know whether the file was accessed, the exact scope, or whether notification is required, and the investigation is "preliminary".

- This is personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires a reasonable and expeditious assessment, ordinarily within 30 days of suspicion. The incident was known by 22 September; an investigation still "preliminary" in November is itself a compliance concern.
- If the data belongs to the Company's customers (likely for an analytics business), there may be contractual notification obligations to those customers (check Bluefen and Mossvale contracts) and, if any data subjects are overseas, foreign regimes (e.g. GDPR).
- Civil penalties for serious interferences with privacy are now very substantial; regulatory and customer-relationship consequences are the real exposure, not the direct cost.

**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion covenant: complete the NDB assessment, make any required OAIC and individual notifications, and provide the Buyer with the investigation report; Buyer right to be consulted.
- **Specific indemnity** (uncapped or separately capped, 6 years) for all loss arising from the incident: regulatory penalties and costs, notification/remediation costs, third-party and customer claims, contract terminations.
- Warranty that there have been no other data incidents and that the Company has complied with the Privacy Act and its customer data obligations.
- If the Bluefen or Mossvale data is involved, link back to B1.

### C2. Sandbar supplier renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 (DD-008, DD-011) – **verify before accepting "ordinary course"**

The Disclosure Letter is explicit that it does *not* say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Points to run down:
- Why three identical AUD 110,000 contracts rather than one? If structured to sit under a materiality threshold, the Buyer's thresholds (A4) must aggregate them.
- "Three **related** supplier renewals": related to each other, or a related-party supplier? If the latter, DD-011 should be checked for Seller/management connections and the arrangements treated as related-party dealings (leakage/price adjustment territory).
- Timing: if entered or renewed after the accounts date/locked-box date, confirm they are within ordinary-course conduct covenants and not prepayments that benefit the Seller.
- Obtain the contracts; confirm termination rights and whether the services are actually required post-Completion.

### C3. Title verification (DD-012)

A share register is the Company's own record, not independent verification. The Seller's letter pointedly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification. Before signing: ASIC company search; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (Riverlark security may extend to the shares); share certificates; constitution (pre-emption rights, transfer restrictions); confirm no options, convertibles or shareholder agreements. Fundamental warranties at full price (A1) plus a clean PPSR/ASIC at Completion.

### C4. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) – lower risk, but close them out

- Lease: a notification obligation on a share sale is cheap to comply with. Seller to give the notification before Completion and deliver a copy; warranty that no landlord consent is required and no default arises. Check for any separate change-of-control provision.
- Mossvale: an assignment restriction is usually not triggered by a share sale, but confirm the actual drafting of DD-009 (some "assignment" clauses define change of control as a deemed assignment). Warranty that no counterparty consent is required and no termination right arises on the change of control, backed by a specific disclosure.

---

## Part D – Price mechanics gaps to confirm

The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" but does not say whether the deal is locked-box or completion accounts. Either way, the definitions of **Debt** and **Transaction Expenses** must expressly include: Riverlark (principal, interest, break costs); DD-005 bonuses plus on-costs; the unpaid Ironquay SOW3 fee; any accrued but unpaid tax; and, if the Sandbar contracts prove to be outside the ordinary course, those amounts. If locked box, leakage must capture the bonuses and any related-party supplier payments.

---

## Summary of recommendations (priority order)

| # | Issue | Position to take |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/title warranties in general cap | **Reject.** 100% of price, 6–7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure. |
| 2 | Riverlark release "following Completion" | **Reject.** Repay at Completion from price; payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables. |
| 3 | Bluefen consent | Buyer-only CP: unconditional consent plus evidence 11.3 conditions met; no adverse amendments; all reasonable endeavours; fallback price protection. |
| 4 | "All limitations apply to all Claims" / exclusive remedy / non-reliance | **Reject.** Limitations apply to general warranty claims only; express carve-outs for fundamental, tax, specific indemnities, fraud, Completion obligations, price adjustments. |
| 5 | Ironquay | Payment and confirmatory assignment before Completion; indemnity broadened to loss of ownership; bank-verify the outstanding amount. |
| 6 | DD-006 privacy incident | Complete NDB assessment pre-Completion; uncapped/separately capped specific indemnity; privacy warranties. |
| 7 | DD-005 bonuses | Treat AUD 420k plus super/payroll tax/on-costs as Transaction Expenses deducted from price via funds flow. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (Cl 8.3) | **Delete**; fallback actual knowledge of named individuals from fairly disclosed matters only. |
| 9 | General data-room disclosure | **Reject**; fair-disclosure standard, specific disclosures against specific warranties, defined searches only. |
| 10 | General cap 20% / covenant strength | Negotiate up (30–50%); require escrow/retention or group guarantee; consider W&I for residual. |
| 11 | Thresholds | Tipping basket, not deductible; aggregate related claims; not applicable to fundamental/tax/indemnities. |
| 12 | Tax and IP | Separate tax indemnity (7 years); higher cap/longer period for IP warranties. |
| 13 | Stale disclosure | Bring-down of warranties and Disclosure Letter at Completion; new matters do not qualify warranties but may trigger termination/price adjustment. |
| 14 | Sandbar renewals | Obtain contracts; confirm related-party status, timing and termination rights before accepting "ordinary course". |
| 15 | Title, lease, Mossvale | Independent ASIC/PPSR verification; lease notification pre-Completion; confirm Mossvale clause wording; warranties for each. |

**Suggested framing for the response to Harbourglass:** The Buyer's willingness to accept a general cap in the 20–30% range is conditional on (a) the fundamental, tax and specific-indemnity carve-outs, (b) Riverlark, Ironquay and the bonuses being cleaned up at or before Completion through the funds flow, (c) Bluefen as a Buyer CP, and (d) deletion of the knowledge and general-disclosure provisions. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter demonstrates that each of these is a live, unresolved issue – which is exactly why they cannot be left to a capped, time-limited warranty claim after Completion.

*This review is based solely on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter; the underlying SPA clauses and data-room documents (DD-002 to DD-012) should be checked against it before positions are finalised.*

- De minimis AUD 25,000 and basket AUD 250,000 (~1.04% of price) are within range, but the basket is drafted as a **deductible** ("only the excess above the basket is recoverable"). Push for a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar).
- Add that **related or series claims aggregate** for de minimis purposes – relevant to Sandbar (3 × AUD 110,000) and any pattern of related losses.
- Thresholds must not apply to fundamental, tax, or specific indemnity claims.

### A5. Time limits (Cl 12.3/13)

- General warranties: 18 months is acceptable only if it captures at least one full audited accounting cycle post-Completion; 24 months is preferable.
- Tax: the later of 7 years and the expiry of the relevant ATO amendment period plus a margin.
- The Seller's statement that tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime" should be rejected. Tax needs a separate indemnity (uncapped or capped at price); IP warranties for an analytics business are core-value warranties and should carry at least a higher cap and longer period, particularly given the Ironquay ownership gap.

### A6. Clause 8.3 Buyer knowledge – **reject**

"No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter **discoverable** from the data room or public records" would:
- impute the knowledge of every adviser, not just the deal team;
- extend to constructive knowledge ("discoverable"), i.e. anything in the data room or on ASIC/PPSR, whether or not anyone actually read it; and
- combined with general disclosure (A7), extinguish every warranty touching an issue raised in DD – which is precisely where the risk is.

The Buyer has priced the deal on the warranties; the warranties should not disappear because the Buyer did its diligence.

**Push back:** Delete 8.3. Fallback: limited to *actual* knowledge of two or three named Buyer individuals, derived solely from matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter, and in any event not applying to the specific indemnities.

### A7. General disclosure of data room and public registers (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2) – **reject; require fair disclosure standard**

- General disclosure of "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room means a buried reference in any document qualifies every warranty.
- "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended (what records, which date?).
- DL 1.4 says nothing in the letter admits that any consent, payment or notice is required – the Seller wants the *facts* to count as disclosure but disclaims the *conclusions*. That is fine only if disclosure is limited to specific disclosures.

**Push back:** Disclosure effective only to the extent **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect on the warranty**. No general disclosure of the data room. Public searches limited to specified ASIC and PPSR searches against the Company on a stated date. Specific disclosures are made against specific numbered warranties.

### A8. Stale disclosure – **require bring-down**

Data-room cut-off 22 September 2026. Require: (i) warranties repeated at Completion; (ii) updated Disclosure Letter at Completion for new matters only, which does **not** qualify warranties for the purpose of a Buyer claim but gives the Buyer a termination right / price adjustment if material; (iii) Seller obligation to notify any breach discovered between signing and Completion.

## Part B – Pre-Completion issues the Seller is trying to push past Completion

### B1. Bluefen change-of-control consent (Cl 3/6.3; DD-002) – **highest commercial priority**

~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue, ~30% of the business. Change-control consent under clause 11.2 is subject to conditions in 11.3. The Disclosure Letter confirms **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions have been satisfied**.

Problems with the Seller's position:
- "Reasonable endeavours" is the weakest endeavours standard.
- Treating the condition as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's "written consent" alone ignores clause 11.3 – a conditional consent whose conditions are unmet is no protection; Bluefen could still terminate.
- Nothing says the consent must be unconditional or on terms acceptable to the Buyer; the Seller could obtain consent by agreeing adverse amendments.

**Push back:**
- Condition precedent for the **Buyer's sole benefit** (waivable only by the Buyer): Bluefen written consent, unconditional or on terms approved by the Buyer, plus evidence that all 11.3 conditions are satisfied, with no amendment to the Bluefen contract without Buyer approval.
- Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours), with Buyer participation in Bluefen discussions, and a sensible long-stop date.
- If the Seller resists a hard CP: price adjustment/earn-out holdback referable to Bluefen revenue, or a specific indemnity/retention if Bluefen terminates or reduces scope within 12–24 months by reason of the change of control.

### B2. Riverlark Bank facility (Cl 2/7; DD-003) – **reject "release following Completion"**

~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, change-of-control clause 8.1, discharge clause 9.2. The deal is debt-free/cash-free, yet the Seller proposes that the release follows Completion. Consequences if accepted:
- The Buyer acquires a company carrying AUD 3.2m of secured debt and likely in change-of-control default from the moment of Completion.
- Riverlark's security (over company assets and possibly the shares – check DD-003 and PPSR) remains in place after the Buyer owns the company.
- No mechanism ensures the Seller ever funds repayment.

**Push back:**
- Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price via the funds flow: bank payout letter (figure as at Completion date) delivered pre-Completion; on Completion, Buyer pays the payout amount directly to Riverlark; delivery of executed deed of release, PPSR discharge and release of any share security as Completion deliverables.
- Any amount not discharged at Completion is Debt for the price mechanism and is deducted dollar-for-dollar.
- Confirm whether Riverlark consent is needed under 8.1 even for a Completion repayment (e.g. prepayment fees, break costs) – these are for the Seller's account.

### B3. Ironquay Development Studio – SOW3 Project Materials (Cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010) – **this is an IP ownership gap, not a AUD 180,000 payment issue**

DD-004 clause 7.3: Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment exist. Until paid, the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables. For an analytics company, that may be core product.

The Seller's indemnity "limited to the specific SOW3 payment" would, at most, reimburse AUD 180,000 – and under the Seller's A3 drafting would be subject to the 20% cap, basket and 18-month limit. It would not cover loss of ownership, third-party claims, injunctions, or re-development cost.

**Push back:**
- Completion deliverable / CP: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay (plus moral-rights consents from individual developers if not already in place).
- Independent verification (bank statements, Ironquay confirmation) of what is actually outstanding – the Seller itself notes DD-010 is not bank-verified.
- Specific indemnity broadened to all loss arising from the Company not owning, or Ironquay asserting rights in, the SOW3 Project Materials – outside the general cap/basket/time limits.
- If the fee is unpaid at Completion, it is Debt in the price mechanism.

### B4. Completion bonuses – DD-005 (AUD 420,000) – **must go into the funds flow**

The bonuses are a **Company** liability triggered by Completion. "A matter for the Seller and not separately itemised" means, in practice, the Company (now Buyer-owned) pays them after Completion. In addition, the Disclosure Letter confirms on-costs are unquantified: superannuation (12% from 1 July 2025), NSW payroll tax (5.45% above threshold), and any leave or workers-comp loading – realistically AUD 480,000–500,000 all-in.

**Push back:**
- Bonuses plus all on-costs are **Transaction Expenses/Debt** deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller through the funds flow at Completion with evidence of payment.
- Review DD-005 terms: who are the recipients, is "continued employment" a condition at Completion or for a period after (if after, the Company bears a contingent liability and retention risk), and is there any claw-back.
- Warranty that there are no other transaction-related payments, change-of-control entitlements, or accelerated equity.

## Part C – Operational and compliance matters characterised as immaterial

### C1. DD-006 export/privacy incident – **specific indemnity required; "not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion**

Download link sent to an unintended external email address; ~1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps. The Seller does not know whether the file was accessed, the exact scope, or whether notification is required, and the investigation is "preliminary".

- This is personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires a reasonable and expeditious assessment, ordinarily within 30 days of suspicion. The incident was known by 22 September; an investigation still "preliminary" in November is itself a compliance concern.
- If the data belongs to the Company's customers (likely for an analytics business), there may be contractual notification obligations to those customers (check Bluefen and Mossvale contracts) and, if any data subjects are overseas, foreign regimes (e.g. GDPR).
- Civil penalties for serious interferences with privacy are now very substantial; regulatory and customer-relationship consequences are the real exposure, not the direct cost.

**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion covenant: complete the NDB assessment, make any required OAIC and individual notifications, and provide the Buyer with the investigation report; Buyer right to be consulted.
- **Specific indemnity** (uncapped or separately capped, 6 years) for all loss arising from the incident: regulatory penalties and costs, notification/remediation costs, third-party and customer claims, contract terminations.
- Warranty that there have been no other data incidents and that the Company has complied with the Privacy Act and its customer data obligations.
- If the Bluefen or Mossvale data is involved, link back to B1.

### C2. Sandbar supplier renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 (DD-008, DD-011) – **verify before accepting "ordinary course"**

The Disclosure Letter is explicit that it does *not* say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Points to run down:
- Why three identical AUD 110,000 contracts rather than one? If structured to sit under a materiality threshold, the Buyer's thresholds (A4) must aggregate them.
- "Three **related** supplier renewals": related to each other, or a related-party supplier? If the latter, DD-011 should be checked for Seller/management connections and the arrangements treated as related-party dealings (leakage/price adjustment territory).
- Timing: if entered or renewed after the accounts date/locked-box date, confirm they are within ordinary-course conduct covenants and not prepayments that benefit the Seller.
- Obtain the contracts; confirm termination rights and whether the services are actually required post-Completion.

### C3. Title verification (DD-012)

A share register is the Company's own record, not independent verification. The Seller's letter pointedly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification. Before signing: ASIC company search; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (Riverlark security may extend to the shares); share certificates; constitution (pre-emption rights, transfer restrictions); confirm no options, convertibles or shareholder agreements. Fundamental warranties at full price (A1) plus a clean PPSR/ASIC at Completion.

### C4. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) – lower risk, but close them out

- Lease: a notification obligation on a share sale is cheap to comply with. Seller to give the notification before Completion and deliver a copy; warranty that no landlord consent is required and no default arises. Check for any separate change-of-control provision.
- Mossvale: an assignment restriction is usually not triggered by a share sale, but confirm the actual drafting of DD-009 (some "assignment" clauses define change of control as a deemed assignment). Warranty that no counterparty consent is required and no termination right arises on the change of control, backed by a specific disclosure.

## Part D – Price mechanics gaps to confirm

The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" but does not say whether the deal is locked-box or completion accounts. Either way, the definitions of **Debt** and **Transaction Expenses** must expressly include: Riverlark (principal, interest, break costs); DD-005 bonuses plus on-costs; the unpaid Ironquay SOW3 fee; any accrued but unpaid tax; and, if the Sandbar contracts prove to be outside the ordinary course, those amounts. If locked box, leakage must capture the bonuses and any related-party supplier payments.

| # | Issue | Position to take |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/title warranties in general cap | **Reject.** 100% of price, 6–7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure. |
| 2 | Riverlark release "following Completion" | **Reject.** Repay at Completion from price; payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables. |
| 3 | Bluefen consent | Buyer-only CP: unconditional consent plus evidence 11.3 conditions met; no adverse amendments; all reasonable endeavours; fallback price protection. |
| 4 | "All limitations apply to all Claims" / exclusive remedy / non-reliance | **Reject.** Limitations apply to general warranty claims only; express carve-outs for fundamental, tax, specific indemnities, fraud, Completion obligations, price adjustments. |
| 5 | Ironquay | Payment and confirmatory assignment before Completion; indemnity broadened to loss of ownership; bank-verify the outstanding amount. |
| 6 | DD-006 privacy incident | Complete NDB assessment pre-Completion; uncapped/separately capped specific indemnity; privacy warranties. |
| 7 | DD-005 bonuses | Treat AUD 420k plus super/payroll tax/on-costs as Transaction Expenses deducted from price via funds flow. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (Cl 8.3) | **Delete**; fallback actual knowledge of named individuals from fairly disclosed matters only. |
| 9 | General data-room disclosure | **Reject**; fair-disclosure standard, specific disclosures against specific warranties, defined searches only. |
| 10 | General cap 20% / covenant strength | Negotiate up (30–50%); require escrow/retention or group guarantee; consider W&I for residual. |
| 11 | Thresholds | Tipping basket, not deductible; aggregate related claims; not applicable to fundamental/tax/indemnities. |
| 12 | Tax and IP | Separate tax indemnity (7 years); higher cap/longer period for IP warranties. |
| 13 | Stale disclosure | Bring-down of warranties and Disclosure Letter at Completion; new matters do not qualify warranties but may trigger termination/price adjustment. |
| 14 | Sandbar renewals | Obtain contracts; confirm related-party status, timing and termination rights before accepting "ordinary course". |
| 15 | Title, lease, Mossvale | Independent ASIC/PPSR verification; lease notification pre-Completion; confirm Mossvale clause wording; warranties for each. |

**Suggested framing for the response to Harbourglass:** The Buyer's willingness to accept a general cap in the 20–30% range is conditional on (a) the fundamental, tax and specific-indemnity carve-outs, (b) Riverlark, Ironquay and the bonuses being cleaned up at or before Completion through the funds flow, (c) Bluefen as a Buyer CP, and (d) deletion of the knowledge and general-disclosure provisions. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter demonstrates that each of these is a live, unresolved issue – which is exactly why they cannot be left to a capped, time-limited warranty claim after Completion.

*This review is based solely on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter; the underlying SPA clauses and data-room documents (DD-002 to DD-012) should be checked against it before positions are finalised.*
